text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A woman is killed in a shootout between police and four suspected gangsters in Nairobi's slum area of Kiamaiko.
- Eleven members of parliament from North Eastern province ask the government to declare the region a disaster zone to attract donor relief food.
- Chaos, confusion and frustration continue to mount in most Identity Card (ID) registration centres countrywide as thousands of citizens rush to beat the Jan 31 deadline for new generation IDs.
- Civil servants are demanding a 500 percent increase on their monthly salaries from the government.
- The Presbyterian Church of East Africa has picked Reverend Jesse Macharia Kamau as the new moderator.
- James Songok, a director of the dairy Kenya Co-Operative Creameries, says the milk body could collapse due to petty differences among board members and a weak tendering system.
- A primary school leaver who was lured into accepting "salvation" is now bed-ridden after her chest was almost roasted by salvation flames prescribed by a priest.
- The managing director of Nzoia Sugar Company and three top executives are remanded by a Nairobi court for conspiring to defraud the government of 904,000 shillings.
